rounds.text: Aspinwall & Company Ltd is currently trading at a significant discount to its intrinsic value, with a price-to-book ratio of 0.91x [E2] and an EV/EBITDA of 8.24x, both of which sit well below their respective sector benchmarks of 1.42x and 10.57x [E7, E11]. The company is demonstrating a clear inflection point in performance, evidenced by a 28% growth in trailing twelve-month sales [E17] and a 57% surge in profit growth over the same period [E21]. This momentum is further supported by a margin of safety of 21.7% based on a discounted cash flow analysis [E45]. While the company maintains a healthy dividend payout of 39.2% [E60], it is also successfully expanding its operating margins, which have improved by 1 percentage point over the last three years [E29]. Conceded: the company faces challenges with negative operating cash flow [E33, E34] and inconsistent profit growth trends over the longer term [E18, E20]. Despite these hurdles, the stock currently trades at a level that implies only 0.5% earnings growth, failing to account for the company's recent operational improvements [E46].

Aspinwall & Company Ltd is currently trading at a significant discount to its intrinsic value, with a price-to-book ratio of 0.91x [E2] and a market price of ₹ 235 against a DCF-derived intrinsic value of ₹ 300 [E44]. The company is demonstrating a powerful operational turnaround, evidenced by trailing twelve-month sales growth of 28% [E17] and a massive 57% surge in compounded profit growth over the same period [E21]. This momentum is further supported by an expansion in operating margins, which have improved by 1 percentage point over the last three years [E29] and by 3 percentage points in the most recent quarter [E30]. The stock is currently undervalued relative to its sector, trading at an EV/EBITDA of 8.24x compared to the sector benchmark of 10.57x [E11]. Conceded: the company faces challenges with negative operating cash flow [E33, E34] and inconsistent long-term profit growth [E18, E20]. Despite these hurdles, the rules-based screen assigns a score of 72 out of 100, reflecting a positive outlook driven by the recent acceleration in top and bottom-line performance [E64, E67].
